text: The fluorescence probe (4-dimethylaminochalcone; DMH) was covalently linked to human serum albumin (HSA). The variation of pH was due to structural changes in HSA, which was determined in terms of DMH and HSA fluorescence and CD spectra. Considerable changes of fluorescence and CD spectra were observed at pH 8 and 10, where there is ionization of two more recently titrated tyrosin residues. It is assumed that these two tyrosine residues are in the binding region and quench the fluorescence of DMH between pH 4 to 8. Quenching disappears if these residues are ionized (pH greater than 8) or if the protein undergoes the N-F transition (pH less than 4).
